title: a file that ends inside a fenced code block gets no block (exit 3), because the block would be quoted and every run would add another
source: intended: docs/decisions.md D8 (setup instructions, defect N-18): a delimited, reversible JITSO block in the instruction files agents read
intent: INTENDED behavior (defect N-18, setup instructions). `AGENTS.md` opens a fenced code block at line 3 and never closes it, and has no block. Appending would put the block inside the fence, where it is not recognized, so the next run would append again. The command refuses: exit 3, `jitso: AGENTS.md ends inside a code fence that starts at line 3; close the fence by hand; nothing written`, the file untouched.

stderr.equals: jitso: AGENTS.md ends inside a code fence that starts at line 3; close the fence by hand; nothing written
